summary: A Victorian Gothic brick light on Mohegan Bluff, lit in 1875 and hauled 245 feet inland in 1993 to keep it from falling into the sea.

access.note: Grounds open daily sunrise to sunset; tower by guided tour only; museum and tours seasonal, closed in winter (Foundation website, accessed 2026-10-22).

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on tower height (52 ft vs 67 ft), focal height (201 vs 204 ft), 1906 (1984 NRHP) vs 1907 (NHL) for the incandescent oil vapor lamp (not used in story), and keeper dates (USLHS vs Foundation list: Dodge 1922 vs 1923; Clark 1930 vs 1931). The NHL nomination says 'fixed green' 1929-1991, which contradicts its own flashing description; not used. Keepers roster is the USLHS list with person slugs; Uriah D. Dodge added from the Foundation list; the Foundation also names Chad E./Bauis E. Dodge, J. W. Tourgee, Lewis Schutt and others whose spellings differ from USLHS (Tourjee, Schlitt) and were not added as separate lines. No newspaper or LHB reports before 1891 are in the corpus; the 1899 report was read by scan page (printed page not confirmed). 1,003 fog-signal hours is for fiscal year ended June 30, 1899. Lighthouse Friends (copyright) used for facts only (Palmetto 1858, Sheffield purchase, cost, siren 1874, tower height). The Foundation page is a modern copyrighted site that reproduces a 2005 Providence Journal article and an 1893 guidebook; both are cited second-hand to that page. Current ownership/hours taken from the Foundation website as of 2026-10-22; current light characteristic not researched. Chronicling America search found no relevant pages. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Light-House Board 1899 fog-signal hours are on scan page 116, telephone/Coast Signal entry on scan page 104 (printed pages not confirmed).
